calls.head: Expect the Avalanche to have the puck more
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Avalanche have been the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Flyers one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Avalanche’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.
calls.call: The Avalanche get the bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 30% chance, and they proved us wrong.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 70% chance, but Philadelphia had other ideas.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Zegras has three assists as the Flyers beat the Avalanche
paras: Matvei Michkov got the scoring started for the Flyers on the power play early in the first, and the goal stood after the Avalanche challenged for goalie interference. Michkov scored his second of the night midway through the second to make it 2-0, but Martin Nečas got the Avs on the board late in the period. Noel Acciari scored his first goal for Philadelphia early in the third to make it 3-1 for the Flyers, and that one stood up as the winner. T.J. Hughes pulled the Avalanche within one with less than six minutes left. Trevor Zegras finished with three assists.

The Flyers had a bit more of the good stuff. The Avalanche hit two posts and still lost. Joseph Woll made 24 saves for the Flyers, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 21 of 24 at the other end. The Flyers improved to 2-6-3 and climbed off the bottom of the Metropolitan to seventh, while the Avalanche dropped to 5-3-1, third in the Central.

items.text: Noah Juulsen played his first game back in Philadelphia.
Matvei Michkov has scored in three straight games.

The Flyers won without Owen Tippett, Tyson Foerster, Rasmus Ristolainen and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Wild and the Sabres were missing more at the time.
The Flyers have won two of their last ten.
